/-!
# Erdős Problem 398

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/398](https://www.erdosproblems.com/398)
 - [Wikipedia: Brocard's problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_problem)
-/

open Nat

namespace Erdos398

/--
**Brocard's Problem**
Does $n! + 1 = m^2$ have integer solutions other than $n = 4, 5, 7$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_398 : answer(sorry) ↔ {n | ∃ m, n ! + 1 = m ^ 2} = {4, 5, 7} := by
  sorry

end Erdos398

findings.description: The docstring asks whether there are solutions other than n = 4, 5, 7, whereas the Lean answer is positive exactly when there are no other solutions. The known solutions make these propositions negations of one another, as independently proved in the scratch files. This is a documentation polarity mismatch, not a defect in the underlying mathematics: the Lean body correctly expresses Erdős’s original only-solutions question.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia’s question box asks, “Does n!+1=m² have integer solutions other than n=4,5,7?” Its Brown numbers section also states that Erdős conjectured that no other solutions exist. The linked primary reference, Erdős, Quelques problèmes de la théorie des nombres (1963), problème 67, p. 129, explicitly asks whether the listed solutions are the only ones: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to: “Are n = 4, 5, 7 the only values of n for which n! + 1 = m² has an integer solution m?” Keep the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean specifies the set of natural-number n admitting a natural-number square root, rather than listing the three solution pairs; Wikipedia describes integer solutions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The pairs (4,5), (5,11), and (7,71) satisfy the equation. Conversely, once n is one of 4, 5, 7, uniqueness of a nonnegative square root forces m to be 5, 11, or 71 respectively. Integer witnesses can be replaced by their natural absolute values without changing their squares. Allowing n = 0 adds nothing because 0! + 1 = 2 is not a square. Independent Lean proofs establish the pair-classification equivalence, natural/integer witness equivalence, and positivity of solution indices.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Quelques problèmes de la théorie des nombres (1963), introduction and problème 67, pp. 129–130: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1963-14.pdf
review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. The accessible sources continue to describe the problem as open. The live erdosproblems.com page and its LaTeX endpoint returned Cloudflare HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so their exact current wording and status could not be checked; the other cited source and its linked primary reference were read instead. Scratch files under /workspace/review/ verify the equivalences and boundary cases, including a computed search through n = 50 yielding exactly [4, 5, 7]. The reviewed file was not modified.
